children: Firmus Grid is seeking $3 billion through private equity, debt and customer prepayments after abandoning its planned stock market listing, the Australian Financial Review reported, citing three people familiar with the matter.

For investors, the fundraising highlights the financing pressures facing AI infrastructure developers as concerns about valuations and borrowing costs weaken demand for public offerings. Customer advances could help Firmus finance expansion, although the proposed package also includes borrowing and new shares.
Prepayment discussions involving customers including Nvidia
, an existing backer, and Meta Platforms
are the furthest advanced, according to the report. The arrangements could allow Firmus to collect 12.5% of its contract payments upfront to support additional AI computing and data center capacity.
Firmus withdrew its IPO last month amid insufficient investor demand. The offering targeted a $30 billion valuation and sought to raise as much as $5.5 billion, including an overallotment option.
In September, Firmus and Meta announced agreements for AI computing capacity at Firmus’s planned Southeast Asian facilities.
